title: Inference Endpoint Collection PRD + Launch Playbook (chat / completions / embeddings / rerank)
creator: Ava Chen
description: PRD and launch playbook to deliver a unified, production-grade hosted endpoint collection for chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank. This work defines API contracts, acceptance criteria, rollout strategy, and operational readiness checks so teams can ship the consolidated surface with SLAs and minimal breaking changes.
background: Customers have requested a single predictable inference surface that supports streaming chat, structured completions, high-throughput embeddings, and reranking pipelines. Internally we maintain multiple overlapping endpoints with divergent defaults which increases developer confusion and operational toil. This initiative consolidates the surface while preserving backward compatibility where possible and defining clear migration paths.
goals: Provide a single documented endpoint family that supports chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank use cases
Define stable API contracts and sensible defaults for latency/cost trade-offs
Ship launch playbook with monitoring, SLOs, and rollback criteria
Ensure migration guidance and compatibility for existing customers
non_goals: Replacing customers' self-hosted/private deployments (Private/Dedicated are out of scope for this ticket)
Major model architecture changes or training (model onboarding is separate)
Extensive SDK language bindings updates beyond minimal surfaced compatibility notes
user_stories: As a product engineer, I can call a single endpoint to run streaming chat with function/tool calling enabled
As a data scientist, I can create high-throughput embedding batches with a predictable per-token cost estimate
As an SRE, I can monitor per-route latency and error budgets and trigger automatic rollback on regression
As a platform customer, I can migrate from legacy endpoints using a documented compatibility shim
api_surface: /v1/hosted/chat: streaming + messages array + function calling + structured output via schema parameter
/v1/hosted/complete: non-streaming completions, prompt templates, temperature/top-p, stop sequences
/v1/hosted/embeddings: batch input, per-item metadata, batching hints, async job support
/v1/hosted/rerank: pairwise and list scoring modes, optional feature vectors, top-k retrieval integration
backward_compatibility: Maintain compatibility shims for the top two existing legacy endpoints. Default parameter mappings will be provided and documented. Breaking changes are allowed only with explicit migration guides and a 3-month deprecation window. Any user-visible default change must be gated behind a feature flag for enterprise tenants.
acceptance_criteria: All four endpoint paths implement documented request/response contracts and validation schemas and return 4xx for invalid requests
Streaming chat has <100ms first-byte latency for warm connections under P50 on the hosted tier (internal perf benchmark)
Embeddings endpoint supports batch sizes up to 4096 vectors per request with linear memory scaling and documented cost model
Rerank produces deterministic ranking for same input with a stability delta <= 0.5% across canary vs prod models
API schema and OpenAPI spec checked into docs repo and accessible via /openapi.json
End-to-end tests (unit + integration + canary smoke) pass in CI for all endpoints
Security review completed and KMS encryption at rest confirmed for any persisted payloads
Feature flags and rollout gates are implemented: gradual ramp with canary controls and automated rollback triggers
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Internal): SDK and endpoint mocks deployed to staging; internal developers invited to trial
Phase 1 (Canary): 2% traffic routed through new surface for non-critical customers for 72 hours
Phase 2 (Gradual Ramp): 10% -> 50% over 7 days contingent on SLOs and error budgets
Phase 3 (Wide): 100% routing for supported hosted customers with opt-out for legacy paths
Rollback criteria: error rate increase > 0.8% absolute or P95 latency regression > 30% sustained over 15 minutes
launch_checklist: PRD and acceptance criteria reviewed and signed off by PM, Eng lead, and Design
SDK compatibility notes added to SDK repo and docs
End-to-end and canary tests green in CI, with performance benchmarks attached
Observability dashboards created: per-route latency, token throughput, cost per request, error breakdown
SLO & alert rules created in PagerDuty/Prometheus with runbooks
Security review completed and any remediation tickets closed
Customer migration guide published with examples and a compatibility shim code sample
Billing impacts verified: cost model updated and examples in pricing docs
Support runbook created for Tier 1/2 with escalation matrix
Legal/compliance checklist (DSA/GDPR considerations) completed for EU customers
Stakeholder communications drafted: blog draft, release notes, changelog entry
monitoring_and_slo: SLO: 99.5% success rate per route per day
SLO: P95 latency targets — chat streaming first-byte <120ms, completion <250ms, embeddings batch <400ms
Traces per request captured with model-version and routing-decision tags
Cost telemetry: per-token median cost and 95th percentile cost per client ID
Automated healthcheck: synthetic traffic for each route every 60s with synthetic latency thresholds
dependencies: Serving runtime: kernel selection patch v2.11 (ENG-5129)
Billing: metering update to support embeddings per-vector units (FIN-88)
SDK: minor changes to streaming interface (SDK-72)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Latency regression under real-world mixed workloads. Mitigation: canary + real traffic shadowing + automatic fallback to legacy variant
Risk: Unexpected cost increase for customers due to larger default batch sizes. Mitigation: conservative defaults, visible cost-estimation in response headers
Risk: Data residency/compliance gaps for EU customers. Mitigation: block EU customers by default until region flags validated, coordinate with Private team for on-prem options
Risk: Breaking client SDKs. Mitigation: maintain compatibility layer for 3 months and provide migration helper scripts
open_questions: Do we expose a single combined pricing SKU for the endpoint family or keep per-capability pricing? (finance decision required)
Should the rerank endpoint accept pre-computed feature vectors exclusively or allow server-side featurization?
What is the acceptable default max token limit for completions to balance cost and UX?
Which early adopter customers will be invited to the canary program and what data-sharing agreements are required?
